title: Checkpoint after conflict-free decisions without revisiting cleared cycles
narrative: After a decision is settled, the nodes it still conflicts with are revisited, and nodes already visited are not revisited so a circular conflict cannot loop forever. A checkpoint is taken only when the decision has no remaining conflicts; a conflict blocked only by the visited set is reported instead of silently saved. The conflicts themselves are still the write-scope conflicts the product already detects (`fangore_transactional_durable_resume`, `fangore_decision_plane_policy`); this adds the revisit-and-checkpoint rule on top. Tracks MH-SR-08[^insp-sr-08].
implementation: `neighbors_from_write_conflicts()` and `neighbor_revisit()` in `decision_conflict_checkpoint.py` are pure functions over `ExecutionGraph.concurrent_write_conflicts` output and a visited set: they return the next nodes to revisit, the skipped visited neighbors, `checkpoint` (conflicts cleared) and `cycle_blocked`. Not a second conflict-resolution engine; hosts still checkpoint through `CheckpointStore` and halt via `StopContract`.
validation: Kind `decision_conflict_neighbor_revisit`. Hard expects, over a chain of write-scope conflicts, the visit order, that a cyclic conflict terminates without a checkpoint and reports the cycle block, and that a cleared decision checkpoints. Unit tests: `tests/test_decision_conflict_checkpoint.py`.
